nodes.name: Image macro
nodes.summary: A picture with bold caption text laid over it, the oldest and broadest family of internet memes.

nodes.name: Object labelling
nodes.summary: A single image whose people or objects are tagged with labels so the scene stands for an unrelated situation.

nodes.name: Reaction image
nodes.summary: A still image, usually a face, posted as a reply to show how the poster feels about something.

nodes.name: Drawn character
nodes.summary: A recurring hand-drawn figure that stands in for a mood or a social type and is endlessly redrawn by others.

nodes.name: Comparison
nodes.summary: A layout that sets two or more panels side by side to contrast options, people or outcomes.

nodes.name: Exploitable
nodes.summary: A source image built so that one part can be swapped or redrawn, inviting endless edits.

nodes.name: Multi-panel comic
nodes.summary: A short strip of sequential panels that tells a joke through a small recurring cast.

nodes.name: Copypasta
nodes.summary: A block of text copied and reposted verbatim or with small edits across forums and comment threads.

nodes.name: Catchphrase
nodes.summary: A short phrase that spreads on its own and is attached to many different images and situations.

nodes.name: Video remix
nodes.summary: A video clip or soundtrack that is re-edited, overdubbed or recombined into new versions.

nodes.name: Wojak
nodes.summary: A simple line drawing of a bald, sad-eyed man used to express longing, regret or quiet melancholy, and the base for a large cast of redrawn variants.

nodes.name: I Know That Feel Bro
nodes.summary: Two Wojaks hugging under the line 'I know that feel bro', posted in reply to a story of shared misfortune.

nodes.name: Crying Wojak
nodes.summary: A red-faced Wojak with tears and clenched teeth, used to depict someone furious or upset at an outcome.
nodes.check_note: Earliest known use is an unsourced comic believed to date from 2014; year is soft. Looked for a non-Know-Your-Meme source for this 2014 date; the Daily Dot's own Wojak coverage cites Know Your Meme for it rather than confirming it independently, so it is left unconfirmed.

nodes.name: Wojak Mask
nodes.summary: A crying Wojak holding a smiling mask over his face, used to show someone hiding distress behind a cheerful front.

nodes.name: Pink Wojak
nodes.summary: A pink, screaming Wojak used on trading and crypto boards to depict panic during a market crash.

nodes.name: Brainlet
nodes.summary: A Wojak drawn with a shrunken head or tiny brain, used to mock a take as unintelligent.
nodes.check_note: The term 'brainlet' is first archived on 4chan /sci/ in December 2015; the Wojak image may only date from 2016. Looked for a non-Know-Your-Meme source confirming either date; found none, so this is left unconfirmed.

nodes.name: Big Brain Wojak
nodes.summary: A bespectacled Wojak with a hugely enlarged, wrinkled brain, used ironically for overthought or self-satisfied reasoning.

nodes.name: NPC Wojak
nodes.summary: A grey, expressionless Wojak used to cast people as non-player characters who repeat opinions without thinking.

nodes.name: Thirty-Year-Old Boomer
nodes.summary: A sunglasses-wearing Wojak holding an energy drink, mocking a young adult with the tastes and habits of an older generation.

nodes.name: Zoomer
nodes.summary: A youthful Wojak representing a teenage member of Generation Z and their online habits.

nodes.name: Doomer
nodes.summary: A Wojak in a black beanie and hoodie, often smoking, representing a young man resigned to hopelessness about the future.

nodes.name: Doomer Girl
nodes.summary: A female counterpart to the Doomer, drawn in dark clothes with short black hair, sharing his gloomy outlook.

nodes.name: Bloomer
nodes.summary: A content, smiling Wojak created as the hopeful opposite of the Doomer.

nodes.name: Coomer
nodes.summary: A dishevelled, hollow-eyed Wojak used to mock someone ruled by compulsive habits, originally pornography.
nodes.check_note: Dictionary.com dates the first Coomer image to a 4chan thread in December 2018.

nodes.name: Consoomer
nodes.summary: A Wojak variant mocking someone whose identity revolves around buying franchise products and merchandise.

nodes.name: Soyjak
nodes.summary: A bearded, bespectacled Wojak with a wide open-mouthed expression, used to caricature naive or performative excitement.

nodes.name: Two Soyjaks Pointing
nodes.summary: Two excited Soyjaks pointing at something placed between them, used to mock overexcitement about a product or reveal.

nodes.name: Yes Chad
nodes.summary: A calm, bearded blond figure who answers a mocking question with a flat 'Yes.', used to show unashamed confidence.
nodes.check_note: Character parent Wojak follows the fixture; Chad is a credible alternative. Format parent Virgin vs. Chad is by analogy (insecure vs confident archetypes): the documented origin (Aug 2019) combines the Grayons meme with a 4chan Nordic/Mediterranean exploitable. Fallback format parent: comparison. MEL Magazine confirms the character grew out of 2016 4chan /pol/ Nordic-vs-Mediterranean discussions and had reached its 'Yes' format 'by 2019', but does not give an August 2019 posting date, so that specific date is unconfirmed.

nodes.name: Trad Girl
nodes.summary: A blonde, braided female Wojak in a sundress used to depict an idealised traditionalist woman.

nodes.name: Grug
nodes.summary: A caveman Wojak who speaks in broken, simple sentences, used to argue for blunt common sense over sophistication.
nodes.check_note: Earliest illustration reported October 2017; first widely seen upload February 2019. The fixtures call this node 'grug-early-man'. Looked for a non-Know-Your-Meme source for the October 2017 illustration date; found none, so it is left unconfirmed.

nodes.name: Doge
nodes.summary: A photo of the Shiba Inu Kabosu glancing sideways, surrounded by multicoloured Comic Sans phrases in broken English such as 'such wow'.
nodes.check_note: Wikipedia confirms both the Kabosu photo and the earliest dog-photo use of the misspelling 'doge' (an October 2010 Reddit post) date to 2010, while the Comic Sans 'such wow' caption format spread mainly in 2012-2013. Root changed from reaction-image to image-macro.

nodes.name: Cheems
nodes.summary: A different Shiba Inu, Balltze, cast as a feeble Doge-like character whose speech adds stray 'm' sounds, as in 'cheemsburbger'.

nodes.name: Swole Doge
nodes.summary: Doge's head on a heavily muscled body, used to stand for strength and an idealised past.

nodes.name: Swole Doge vs. Cheems
nodes.summary: A two-panel image pitting muscular Swole Doge against small, weak Cheems to contrast a strong past with a feeble present.
nodes.check_note: Format parent Virgin vs. Chad is by analogy (strong vs weak contrast) and not documented as a direct derivation; fallback format parent: comparison. The Daily Dot dates the component characters to 2019 (Cheems June 8, Swole Doge July 7) but gives no date for when the two were first paired, so the reported February 2020 date for the comparison format remains unconfirmed.

nodes.name: Dogelore
nodes.summary: Deliberately misspelled comics that place Doge and an extended cast of dogs in absurd everyday stories.

nodes.name: Walter
nodes.summary: A close-up of a white bull terrier staring into the camera, captioned as loving fire trucks and 'moster trucks'.
nodes.check_note: Film Daily confirms the Nelson/Walter photo was first posted to Twitter in September 2018, independently of Know Your Meme. He is Nelson, a bull terrier, not a Shiba; the character link to Doge records cast membership in Dogelore, not descent, and alternatives are a parent of Dogelore or a standalone family under reaction-image.

nodes.name: Doge Bonk
nodes.summary: Doge swinging a bat at another dog with the word 'bonk', posted to playfully punish an out-of-line remark.

nodes.name: Pepe the Frog
nodes.summary: A green cartoon frog from Matt Furie's comic Boy's Club that became one of the most reused reaction characters online.

nodes.name: Feels Good Man
nodes.summary: Pepe's contented line from the original comic, reused as a caption or emote for simple satisfaction.

nodes.name: Sad Frog
nodes.summary: A dejected, teary Pepe posted to express disappointment, often captioned 'feels bad man'.
nodes.check_note: The University of Luxembourg's HIVI project dates the sad 'Feels bad man' Pepe variant to 2009, earlier than Wikipedia's 'by 2012' Tumblr-usage date.

nodes.name: Smug Frog
nodes.summary: A self-satisfied Pepe with a knowing smirk, posted to gloat or feign superiority.
nodes.check_note: Wikipedia's Pepe the Frog article dates the Smug Pepe variant to 2012; a claimed June 2011 4chan /tv/ post could not be confirmed on any non-Know-Your-Meme source.

nodes.name: Angry Pepe
nodes.summary: A red-faced, shouting Pepe paired with a long 'REEE' to mock an outburst of frustration.

nodes.name: Rare Pepe
nodes.summary: Original or unusual Pepe drawings presented ironically as rare collectibles to be hoarded and traded.

nodes.name: Apu Apustaja
nodes.summary: A deliberately crude, childlike redraw of Pepe whose name is broken Finnish for 'help helper', spread from the Finnish board Ylilauta.

nodes.name: Peepo
nodes.summary: A small, round, simplified Pepe used as a family of Twitch and Discord emotes.

nodes.name: Pepega
nodes.summary: A Pepe with a huge nose and gaping mouth used on Twitch to call something or someone foolish.

nodes.name: monkaS
nodes.summary: A sweating, anxious Pepe emote used on Twitch during tense or nerve-wracking moments.

nodes.name: PepeHands
nodes.summary: A crying Pepe with hands raised to his face, used on Twitch to express sadness or mock grief.

nodes.name: Sadge
nodes.summary: A simplified, downcast Pepe emote used in Twitch chat for mild disappointment.
nodes.check_note: Streamscheme dates the Sadge emote's upload to BetterTTV and FrankerFaceZ to January 2020.

nodes.name: Chad
nodes.summary: An idealised, effortlessly confident alpha male archetype, drawn as a tall square-jawed figure.
nodes.check_note: Date is for the drawn Chad figure of Virgin vs. Chad (2017); the slang 'Chad'/'Chad Thundercock' is older (mid-2010s) and may move this date earlier. The Daily Dot's Virgin vs. Chad coverage attributes the 2017 /r9k/ origin to Know Your Meme without independently confirming it, so this remains unconfirmed.

nodes.name: Virgin vs. Chad
aliases: The Virgin Walk vs. The Chad Stride
nodes.summary: A side-by-side drawing contrasting a hunched, insecure 'virgin' with a confident 'Chad', applied to any pair of rival things.

nodes.name: Gigachad
nodes.summary: Stylised black-and-white photos of an impossibly chiselled man, used as the ultimate image of confident masculinity.

nodes.name: Average Fan vs. Average Enjoyer
nodes.summary: A comparison pairing an anxious, sweaty 'fan' with a calm Gigachad 'enjoyer' of the same thing.
nodes.check_note: Year from the March 2021 video spike; still-image versions may be slightly earlier. Looked for a non-Know-Your-Meme source confirming the proposed September 2019 tweet; found none, so that correction is left unconfirmed.

nodes.name: Advice Dog
nodes.summary: A smiling puppy on a rainbow colour-wheel background, captioned with two lines of terrible advice, which started the Advice Animals genre.

nodes.name: Courage Wolf
nodes.summary: A snarling wolf on a colour wheel offering extreme, aggressive motivational advice.

nodes.name: Insanity Wolf
nodes.summary: A wild-eyed wolf on a colour wheel giving deranged, violent advice as an escalation of Courage Wolf.

nodes.name: Socially Awkward Penguin
nodes.summary: A penguin on a blue colour-wheel background captioned with an embarrassing social blunder.

nodes.name: Socially Awesome Penguin
nodes.summary: The same penguin on a red background, captioned with a socially smooth success.

nodes.name: Philosoraptor
nodes.summary: A drawing of a velociraptor pondering, captioned with a pseudo-profound question or pun.

nodes.name: Foul Bachelor Frog
nodes.summary: A frog in a bathrobe captioned with the lazy, unhygienic habits of a single man living alone.

nodes.name: Paranoid Parrot
nodes.summary: A startled parrot captioned with irrational everyday fears and suspicions.
nodes.check_note: Became popular in August 2010; first use may be earlier. Could not open a non-Know-Your-Meme source confirming that August 2010 Tumblr date, so the date is left at year precision, matching the lead's own caution that this is a popularisation date.

nodes.name: Success Kid
nodes.summary: A toddler on a beach clenching a fistful of sand, captioned with small personal victories.
nodes.check_note: Wikipedia dates the photo itself to August 2007 but the first captioned meme variant, 'I Hate Sandcastles', to 2011; by the first_seen rule it is the meme, not the photo, that is dated here.

nodes.name: Scumbag Steve
nodes.summary: A photo of a young man in a sideways cap and fur coat captioned with selfish, mooching behaviour.

nodes.name: Good Guy Greg
nodes.summary: A smiling man with a joint captioned with unexpectedly considerate behaviour.

nodes.name: Actual Advice Mallard
nodes.summary: A mallard on a colour wheel offering genuinely useful life tips.

nodes.name: Malicious Advice Mallard
nodes.summary: The same mallard with a red head, offering advice designed to cause harm.

nodes.name: Bad Luck Brian
nodes.summary: An awkward school portrait of a teenager in a plaid vest captioned with absurd strokes of misfortune.

nodes.name: Ridiculously Photogenic Guy
nodes.summary: A marathon photo of a runner looking effortlessly handsome, captioned with things that go easily for good-looking people.

nodes.name: Confession Bear
nodes.summary: A sheepish-looking bear captioned with an embarrassing or unpopular personal admission.

nodes.name: Overly Attached Girlfriend
nodes.summary: A wide-eyed, intensely smiling young woman captioned with clingy, possessive relationship behaviour.

nodes.name: Distracted Boyfriend
nodes.summary: A stock photo of a man turning to look at another woman while his partner glares, with each person labelled to show a shift in loyalty.

nodes.name: Drake Hotline Bling
nodes.summary: Two stacked stills of Drake from the 'Hotline Bling' video, waving away the top caption and approving the bottom one.
nodes.check_note: Wikipedia dates the 'Hotline Bling' video, source of the Drakeposting format, to its October 19, 2015 release.

nodes.name: Skibidi Toilet
nodes.summary: An animated web series by Alexey Gerasimov (YouTube channel DaFuq!?Boom!) about toilet-headed figures warring with camera-headed humanoids; the first 11-second episode was released on February 7, 2023.

nodes.name: Chill Guy
nodes.summary: A smirking anthropomorphic dog in a grey sweater with hands in his pockets, drawn by artist Phillip Banks and posted to Twitter/X on October 4, 2023; it became a mass 'my new character' redraw template in late 2024.

nodes.name: Moo Deng
nodes.summary: A baby pygmy hippopotamus born July 10, 2024 at Khao Kheow Open Zoo near Bangkok; a viral photo of her posted by the zoo's X account on August 26, 2024 touched off fan art and reaction-image edits of her startled expressions.

nodes.name: Grimace Shake
nodes.summary: A purple McDonald's milkshake released June 12, 2023 for mascot Grimace's birthday; a TikTok trend had posters film themselves drinking it, then cut to a scene of them collapsed or 'found dead.'

nodes.name: Nihilist Penguin
nodes.summary: A clip of a lone penguin walking away from its colony in Werner Herzog's 2007 documentary 'Encounters at the End of the World,' re-edited with Herzog's narration and melancholic music; TikToker natur_gamler's January 16, 2026 edit touched off a wave of posts using it to express detached, unbothered resignation.

nodes.name: Shrimp Jesus
nodes.summary: AI-generated images fusing Jesus Christ with shrimp or crabs, posted en masse by Facebook engagement-farming accounts from early 2024, which became the signature example of low-effort 'AI slop.'
nodes.check_note: The fetched Nieman Lab source confirms the images and the engagement-farming context but not an exact first-post date; the March 2024 month comes from an unfetched search snippet.

nodes.name: Studio Ghibli AI Filter
nodes.summary: Following OpenAI's native GPT-4o image-generation rollout in late March 2025, users converted personal photos and memes into Studio Ghibli-style AI art en masse, sparking both a huge viral trend and an artist backlash.

nodes.name: Bombardiro Crocodilo
nodes.summary: An AI-generated hybrid of a military bomber plane and a crocodile, introduced February 20, 2025 as part of the 'Italian Brainrot' wave of AI animal-object hybrid videos narrated in fake Italian.

nodes.name: Tralalero Tralala
nodes.summary: An AI-generated shark wearing Nike sneakers, narrated in fake-Italian text-to-speech gibberish; TikTok creator Choppa (@eZburger401) uploaded the original video in early January 2025, the first of the 'Italian Brainrot' wave.

nodes.name: Absolute Cinema
nodes.summary: A reaction image of director Martin Scorsese raising both hands (from a 2020 New York Times interview photo), captioned 'Absolute Cinema' to praise something as a masterpiece; X user @YashChillinn paired the image with an anime clip in December 2022, and the captioned version spread widely through 2023.

nodes.name: Italian Brainrot
nodes.summary: A 2025 TikTok wave of AI-generated animal-and-object hybrid creatures, each with a sing-song pseudo-Italian name and fake-Italian text-to-speech narration; Tralalero Tralala is widely considered its first example.

nodes.name: Tung Tung Tung Sahur
nodes.summary: An AI-generated wooden log figure holding a bat, named after the drum calls that wake people for sahur, the pre-dawn Ramadan meal; of Indonesian origin, it was absorbed into the Italian Brainrot cast in 2025.
nodes.check_note: Sources give no single creation date; the Indonesian origin and the Ramadan reference agree across sources.

nodes.name: Ballerina Cappuccina
nodes.summary: An AI-generated ballerina with a cappuccino cup for a head, posted by TikTok account @aironic.fun on March 19, 2025, and quickly adopted as an Italian Brainrot character.
nodes.check_note: The date comes from a single meme-aggregator source.

nodes.name: Chimpanzini Bananini
nodes.summary: An AI-generated chimpanzee inside a banana peel, one of the Italian Brainrot characters that spread on TikTok in 2025.

nodes.name: Brr Brr Patapim
nodes.summary: An AI-generated tree-trunk creature with a long nose and big bare feet, part of the 2025 Italian Brainrot cast.

nodes.name: Skibidi
nodes.summary: A Gen Alpha slang word taken from the Skibidi Toilet theme song and used as an all-purpose nonsense intensifier ('skibidi rizz', 'what the skibidi'), part of the 'brainrot' vocabulary.
nodes.check_note: The word spread as slang through 2023 and 2024; no first-use date was found.

nodes.name: Cameraman
nodes.summary: The camera-headed humanoids who fight the singing toilets in Skibidi Toilet; their giant 'Titan Cameraman' became a fan-favourite hero of edits and fan art.
nodes.check_note: Fan sources disagree on which 2023 episode introduced this character; only the year is used.

nodes.name: TV Man
nodes.summary: TV-headed humanoid allies of the Cameramen in Skibidi Toilet who stun toilets with their screens; Titan TV Man became one of the series' most-edited characters.
nodes.check_note: Fan sources disagree on which 2023 episode introduced this character; only the year is used.

nodes.name: Grimace
nodes.summary: A purple, blob-shaped McDonald's mascot from the McDonaldland ads, introduced in 1971 and never clearly defined, which made him an easy target for internet jokes.

nodes.name: That's Not Cinema
nodes.summary: Martin Scorsese's remark to Empire in early October 2019, while promoting 'The Irishman', that Marvel films are 'not cinema' and closer to 'theme parks'; it became a running internet joke about what counts as real cinema.

nodes.name: Haggis
nodes.summary: A female pygmy hippo calf born at Edinburgh Zoo on October 30, 2024; the zoo introduced her with 'Moo Deng? Who deng?', and the press dubbed her 'Scotland's Moo Deng'.

nodes.name: Despicable Me
nodes.summary: Illumination's 2010 animated film about the supervillain Gru and his yellow Minions, whose characters went on to supply several meme families.

nodes.name: Gru's Plan
nodes.summary: A four-panel exploitable template where Gru presents a sequential plan on an easel before doing a shocked double-take at the final step.

nodes.name: Minion Memes
nodes.summary: Captioned images of the Minions delivering jokes, relationship advice and inspirational sayings, ubiquitous on Facebook around the 2015 'Minions' film and widely mocked as the humour of older relatives.
nodes.check_note: The 2015 peak is from memory, not from a fetched source.

nodes.name: Gentleminions
nodes.summary: A July 2022 TikTok trend in which teenagers wore suits to screenings of 'Minions: The Rise of Gru', often to Yeat's 'Rich Minion'; some cinemas turned away suited groups after rowdy showings.

nodes.name: Baby Yoda
nodes.summary: The infant alien from Disney+'s 'The Mandalorian', revealed in the November 12, 2019 premiere; stills of him became one of the most-shared reaction images of late 2019.

nodes.name: Sad Baby Yoda
nodes.summary: A reaction image depicting the Star Wars character Grogu looking dejected or edited with teary eyes, used to express sadness, vulnerability, or disappointment.

nodes.name: Baby Yoda Drinking Soup
nodes.summary: A GIF from 'The Mandalorian' episode 'Sanctuary' (late November 2019) of Baby Yoda slurping broth, used like Kermit sipping tea as a smug 'not my business' reaction.

nodes.name: Duckroll
nodes.summary: A 4chan bait-and-switch prank from late 2006: a promising link led instead to a picture of a duck on wheels. It was named after a word filter that turned 'egg' into 'duck', so 'eggroll' became 'duckroll'.

nodes.name: Rickroll
nodes.summary: A bait-and-switch prank in which an enticing or misleading link unexpectedly directs the viewer to Rick Astley's 1987 music video for 'Never Gonna Give You Up'.

nodes.name: IQ Bell Curve
nodes.summary: A meme template depicting an IQ distribution curve where individuals at the low and high extremes reach the same simple conclusion while the average-IQ midwit overcomplicates it.

nodes.name: Labubu
nodes.summary: A toothy, rabbit-eared elf from Kasing Lung's 2015 picture-book series 'The Monsters', sold as Pop Mart blind-box toys from 2019; after BLACKPINK's Lisa was seen with one in April 2024 it became a global collecting craze and, in 2025, a meme.

nodes.name: Lafufu
nodes.summary: The nickname for counterfeit Labubu dolls, whose off-model faces and wonky teeth made them a joke of their own in 2025.
